## PCI PM callbacks reaching `i915_pm_suspend`

The system-sleep callbacks that funnel into `i915_pm_suspend()` are:

```text
.pci_driver.suspend
  └─> i915_pm_suspend()
        └─> i915_drm_suspend()
              └─> intel_display_suspend()

.pci_driver.freeze
  └─> i915_pm_suspend()
        └─> i915_drm_suspend()
              └─> intel_display_suspend()

.pci_driver.poweroff
  └─> i915_pm_suspend()
        └─> i915_drm_suspend()
              └─> intel_display_suspend()
```

The corresponding wake-up callbacks do not reach `i915_pm_suspend()`:

```text
.resume  ──> i915_pm_resume()
.thaw    ──> i915_pm_resume()
.restore ──> i915_pm_resume()
```

The relevant driver implementation is in:

- `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_driver.c`
- `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_driver.h`
- `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/display/intel_display_driver.c`
- `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/display/intel_display_power.c`

## Callers that also call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`

None of the system-sleep callbacks above directly call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend()` in addition to `i915_pm_suspend()`.

Runtime PM is a separate callback path:

```text
.pci_driver.runtime_suspend
  └─> i915_pm_runtime_suspend()
        ├─> i915_gem_runtime_suspend()
        ├─> intel_gt_runtime_suspend()
        ├─> intel_display_power_suspend()
        └─> intel_uncore_runtime_suspend()
```

Thus:

| PCI callback | Reaches `i915_pm_suspend()` | Also calls `i915_pm_runtime_suspend()` |
|---|---:|---:|
| `suspend` | Yes | No |
| `freeze` | Yes | No |
| `poweroff` | Yes | No |
| `runtime_suspend` | No | It is the runtime-suspend entry point itself |
| `resume` / `thaw` / `restore` | No | No |

The runtime-PM implementation is distributed across:

- `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/intel_runtime_pm.c`
- `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/gem/i915_gem_pm.c`
- `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/gt/intel_gt_pm.c`
- `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/display/intel_display_power.c`
- `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/intel_uncore.c`

## `dev_priv` data flow

The private driver object is obtained from the DRM device in `i915_drm_suspend()` and passed through the display suspend layer:

```text
i915_pm_suspend(struct device *dev)
  └─ drm_device *drm_dev
       └─ i915_drm_suspend(drm_dev)
            └─ struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv =
                   drm_dev->dev_private
                 └─ intel_display_suspend(dev_priv)
                      └─ display state/power handling uses dev_priv
```

Conceptually:

```c
static int i915_drm_suspend(struct drm_device *dev)
{
        struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv = dev->dev_private;

        ...
        intel_display_suspend(dev_priv);
        ...
}
```

No new `dev_priv` object is created along this path. The same `struct drm_i915_private` associated with the `struct drm_device` is recovered once and passed as the display subsystem’s driver-private context.
